Name: Performance HUD - FPS Memory and Debug Display
Author: ZeroXPatch
Description:
[b][color=#ffff00][size=6][center]Customizable Performance/Debug HUD[/center][/size][/color][center]Safe to uninstall anytime. Removing it just disables the features.

[url=https://www.nexusmods.com/profile/ZeroXPatch/mods?gameId=1303&sortBy=downloads]https://www.nexusmods.com/profile/ZeroXPatch/mods?gameId=1303&sortBy=downloads[/url][/center]


Customizable Performance/Debug HUD[/b] adds a lightweight, configurable overlay to Stardew Valley that shows performance and useful debug info in real time.

It’s designed for:

[list]
[*]players who want to monitor FPS/performance,
[*]modders troubleshooting lag or stutter,
[*]streamers/testing setups,
[*]anyone who wants quick “what’s happening right now” info without opening logs.
[/list]All HUD items are individually toggleable in [b]Generic Mod Config Menu (GMCM)[/b], and you can move the HUD with X/Y position settings. You can also bind a hotkey to toggle the HUD on/off instantly.

[b][color=#00ff00]Features[/color]

[/b][list]
[*]FPS + frame time (smoothness / stutter detection)
[*]Memory usage (rough mod load pressure)
[*]Update tick timing (how heavy the game loop is)
[*]Current location ID (helpful for debugging, map mods, and event triggers)
[*]Temporary sprites count (visual effect/activity indicator)
[*]Handy player debug info (tile position, facing direction, date/time, weather, multiplayer)
[/list]
[center][img]https://staticdelivery.nexusmods.com/mods/1303/images/40509/40509-1766536431-871395498.png[/img]﻿﻿[/center]
[list]
[/list][b][color=#00ff00]Configuration[/color][/b]

Open [b]GMCM[/b] → “Customizable Performance/Debug HUD”

[list]
[*]Toggle each stat on/off
[*]Change HUD position (X/Y)
[*]Set a hotkey to toggle the overlay
[/list][b][color=#00ff00]Compatibility

[/color][/b][list]
[*]Safe, overlay-only mod (no saves edited)
[*]Works alongside other mods
[*]No XNB edits
[/list][line][b][color=#00ff00]What each HUD item is for
[/color][/b]
FPS

[b]What it shows:[/b] Frames per second.

[b]Why it matters:[/b]
[list]
[*]Higher FPS generally feels smoother.
[*]If FPS drops hard in certain places (farm, mines, big modded maps), it can tell you [i]where[/i] performance issues happen.
[/list][b]Good for:[/b] “This area feels laggy — is it actually dropping FPS?”
[line]Frame Time (ms)

[b]What it shows:[/b] How long each frame took to render (milliseconds).

[b]Why it matters:
[/b]
[list]
[*]Frame time is [i]the best way to spot stutter[/i].
[*]Even if FPS looks “fine,” frame time spikes reveal hitching/micro-stutter.
[/list][b]Quick rule of thumb:
[/b]
[list]
[*]~16.7ms ≈ 60 FPS
[*]~33.3ms ≈ 30 FPS
Big spikes = stutters.[/list][b]Good for:[/b] “Why does it feel choppy even when FPS says 60?”
[line]Memory

[b]What it shows:[/b] Game process memory usage.

[b]Why it matters:
[/b]
[list]
[*]Heavy mod lists can push memory up.
[*]Large memory usage can correlate with longer loading times, sluggishness, or instability on some systems.
[/list][b]Good for:[/b] “Did adding mods raise memory a lot?” / “Why is my game loading slower?”
[line]Update Load Estimate (Update dt)

[b]What it shows:[/b] How long the game update tick takes (ms), average + max.

[b]Why it matters:
[/b]
[list]
[*]This is a rough indicator of [i]CPU workload per tick[/i].
[*]If this climbs or spikes, it can mean the game is doing too much logic work (often mod-related).
[/list][b]Good for:[/b] “Is the game logic bogging down, not just graphics?”
[line]Location ID

[b]What it shows:[/b] The internal ID/name of the current map.

[b]Why it matters:[/b]
[list]
[*]Helpful for bug reports (“this happens in [b]Town[/b] or [b]Farm[/b] or a modded map name”).
[*]Helps modders debug event conditions, triggers, and map-specific issues.
[/list][b]Good for:[/b] “What map am I actually in?” (especially on custom maps)
[line]Temporary Sprites Count

[b]What it shows:[/b] Count of temporary sprite effects (sparkles, splashes, animations, visual effects).

[b]Why it matters:[/b]
[list]
[*]This number can rise during heavy visual activity (storms, machines, combat, lots of effects).
[*]If it gets unusually high, it can hint that something is spamming effects.
[/list][b]Good for:[/b] “Are visual effects piling up and causing lag?”
[line]Debug QoL

StatsPlayer Tile

[b]What it shows:[/b] Your tile coordinates (X, Y).

[b]Why it matters:[/b]
[list]
[*]Useful for placing things precisely.
[*]Handy when reporting issues to mod authors (“bug occurs at tile 40, 18”).
[/list][b]Good for:[/b] map building, mod debugging, precise placement.
[line]Facing Direction

[b]What it shows:[/b] Which direction you’re facing (Up/Right/Down/Left).

[b]Why it matters:[/b]
[list]
[*]Some interactions, tools, and mod features depend on facing direction.
[*]Useful for debugging “it only works when facing X direction” issues.
[/list][line]In-Game Date/Time

[b]What it shows:[/b] Season/day/year + clock time.

[b]Why it matters:[/b]
[list]
[*]Useful when testing events, schedules, time-based mechanics, or speedruns.
[*]Helps reproduce bugs (“at 9:50 PM on Fall 12”).
[/list][line]Weather

[b]What it shows:[/b] Current weather state (Sun/Rain/Storm/Snow/Wind).

[b]Why it matters:[/b]
[list]
[*]Weather affects NPC routines, lightning behavior, some mod logic, crop watering, etc.
[*]Useful for testing “this only happens in rain/storm”.
[/list][line]Multiplayer Info

[b]What it shows:[/b] Single/Host/Farmhand + player count.

[b]Why it matters:[/b]
[list]
[*]Multiplayer can affect timing, syncing, and certain mod behaviors.
[*]Useful when diagnosing “works in single-player but not multiplayer.”
[/list]

[b][size=4][center][color=#00ff00]Q&A:[/color][/center][/size][/b]
Q: How do I move the HUD?

In GMCM (or [code]config.json[/code]), change:
[list]
[*][code]PositionX[/code]
[*][code]PositionY[/code]
[/list]These are UI pixel coordinates from the top-left corner.

Q: How do I hide/show the HUD quickly?

Use the toggle hotkey in config:
[list]
[*]Default: [b]F8[/b]
You can change it in GMCM under [b]General → Toggle HUD keybind[/b].[/list]Q: My FPS is high but the game still feels stuttery — why?

Check [b]Frame Time[/b].
Even at “60 FPS”, frame time spikes mean micro-stutters/hitches are happening.

Q: What does “Update dt” mean?

That’s the time the game spends per update tick (logic/CPU work), shown as average + max.
Higher values or frequent spikes can indicate heavy logic load (sometimes mod-related).

Q: The numbers look “wrong” or don’t change much. Is it broken?Some values naturally won’t change often:
[list]
[*][b]Location ID[/b] only changes when you change maps.
[*][b]Weather[/b] changes daily.
[*][b]Multiplayer[/b] changes only when players join/leave.
[/list]If [b]everything[/b] is stuck, make sure the HUD is enabled and not toggled off (press your HUD hotkey once).

Q: Will this reduce performance?

Very little. The HUD is lightweight, and most readings are sampled periodically (not every frame).
That said, any overlay adds [i]some[/i] work — if you’re chasing max performance, disable items you don’t need.

Q: Does it work in multiplayer?

Yes. It should work for host and farmhands. The multiplayer line shows your role + player count.

Q: Is it compatible with other UI/HUD mods?

Usually yes. If another mod draws in the same area, just move this HUD using X/Y in GMCM.

Q: Does this work on modded/custom maps?

Yes. Location ID is especially useful for modded maps, since it shows the internal map name.

Q: Can I change font size/colors/anchor?

Not in this version (simple, minimal overlay). If you want these options, request them and I can add:
[list]
[*]scale setting,
[*]anchor presets (TopLeft/TopRight/etc),
[*]optional background opacity,
[*]text color.
[/list]
